what: astroMCBchron() version 2: outlier mixture, laboratory and depth offsets, tempering
title: Changes in version 0.6.0
text: Date model date_model = c("mixture", "two_stage", "gaussian"). default "mixture" gives every date mixture likelihood, (1 - p) x N(date, sd) + p x outlier component, outlier probability p estimated (beta prior outlier_prior, default c(1, 19), mean 0.05) posterior outlier probability every date reported (dates$p_outlier, outlier_prob). outlier component set outlier_type: "scaled" (Gaussian outlier_k x sd), "old" (one-sided: inherited recycled zircon) "young" (one-sided: residual Pb loss). "two_stage" reproduces version 1 (Student-t screening, flagged dates outlier_k x sd); two_stage = TRUE/FALSE still accepted (deprecated). date likelihoods (date_loglik, e.g. upb_grain_loglik()) normalised combined mixture. Weighted-mean dates: optional column dates$mswd; inflate_mswd = TRUE (default) sd dates MSWD > 1 multiplied sqrt(MSWD). Systematic uncertainties: optional columns dates$group (laboratory tracer) dates$tracer_rel. Dates groups anchor get estimated systematic offset prior tracer calibration uncertainty groups (tracer_rel, default 1.5e-4, EARTHTIME ET535/ET2535), astrochronology estimates inter-laboratory offset. tracer term reference group 238U decay-constant term (decay_rel, default 5.4e-4) reported extra envelopes (summary$sd2_tracer_kyr, sd2_total_kyr, lower_tracer, upper_tracer, lower_total, upper_total); affect durations. Depth offsets: dates share dates$depth_group shifted together one estimated offset (prior sd depth_offset_sd), dates whose depths come another depth scale tracks (outcrop samples correlated core, box-label depths). Parallel tempering astronomical part posterior (temper, inverse temperatures starting 1): hot chains can change number cycles dates, alternative solutions found weighted; diagnostics tempering. Leave-one-: date model refitted every run; loo_ids restricts test selected dates. print() plot() show outlier probabilities, group depth offsets tracer total envelopes. misfit placement (misfit, misfit_window) band options version 1 kept unchanged. Tests: test-astroMCBchron-v2.R (date models, outlier types, offsets) test-astroMCBchron-misfit.R.

what: astroMCBchron(): no uncertainty minimum between dates
title: Changes in version 0.6.0
text: New argument misfit = c("localised", "stretch") astroMCBchron(). rigid per-interval stretch ("stretch", earlier behaviour) spreads posterior departure interval’s duration every cycle, age two dates fixed interpolation two uncertain end ages; variance convex smaller dates dates (Tiout: 96-104 kyr , 112-140 kyr dates). "localised" departure sits one horizon unknown position (miscounted cycle, condensed level), makes variance linear dated horizons; unimodal-majorant guard covers hiatuses inside interval Monte Carlo noise 95 % band. MCMC posterior, mean age model, interval durations leave-one-. Stress test (16 random records, 3-7 dates, 0-2 hiatuses): 0 interior minima (stretch: 742), mean 2 sd +3 %. New test test-astroMCBchron-misfit.R. misfit = "window" (new default) misfit_window = 100 (kyr floating time): interval misfit sits one random position, "localised", spread one contiguous window one short-eccentricity cycle instead one step prediction grid; negative misfit compresses window (step loses 70 % time). variance computed exactly window (rigid-stretch variance + 2 (E[F] - w) Cov(a_i, delta) + (E[F^2] - w^2) E[delta^2]). Altajme (paper configuration, MCMC): 2 sd within 3 kyr "localised" (mean outer dates 77.0 77.9 kyr), guard raises 2 sd 0.1 kyr, stored curves keep time everywhere (curves empty step: 0.1 % 96 %; largest one-step departure mean 16 55 kyr, median per curve), can used rate, phase spectral analyses. Durations short events lose heavy tail "localised" (e.g. Ireviken Datum 1 Datum 4: 51 +/- 16 51 +/- 25 kyr). "localised" "stretch" remain available. New argument band = c("analytic", "curves"): 95 % band median summary default analytic mean +/- 1.96 sd (Monte Carlo noise band); percentiles curves returned median_mc, lower_mc, upper_mc, guard_raise_kyr reports much guard raised 2 sd. test-astroMCBchron-misfit.R now also tests "window" (interior minimum, mean, empty steps, within 15 % "localised", analytic band) uses apply-family calls. Ported pending v2 version well (also tracer decay-constant envelopes).

Duration constraints: track_astro_hmm(), track_ridge_hmm() track_astro_auto() accept constraints (data frame , , duration kyr, optional tolerance, default 2.5 %), e.g. radiometric ages well-dated stage boundaries. posterior conditioned constraints (paths drawn tilted posterior, within tolerance kept) best path comes exact constrained Viterbi (elapsed time extra state dimension). Klonk record (Přídolí, 24.8-49.5 m = 4434 kyr) published astrochronology reproduced within 0.3 Myr everywhere Přídolí; without constraint setting . Outside constrained interval (Lochkovian) record decide published three times longer duration: credible band contains confidence low. track_astro_auto(): scalogram = "cwt" (plain Morlet scalogram omega_nr, e.g. 5-6), followed ridges continuously synchrosqueezed maps eccentricity resolved. astro_periods_tracking(include = "eccentricity") gives 405-kyr cycle weight 1 (instead 0.5). what: Even more wavelets, higher-order and superlet synchrosqueezing
title: Changes in version 0.6.0
text: 11 wavelet families (22 total): exactly zero-mean Morlet ("morlet0"), real Morlet ("morl"), Hermitian hat ("hhat"), Poisson, gammatone, Hann (raised cosine), orthogonal Haar, Daubechies ("db1"-"db20"), Symlets ("sym2"-"sym20") Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets, computed frequency domain filters (Daubechies Symlet filters spectral factorisation). PyWavelets style names ("db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2", "cmor1.5-1", "shan2-1.5", "fbsp2-1-1.5") accepted, wavelet can user defined function psi_hat(omega). analyse_wavelet_sst(): sst_order = 2 (second-order synchrosqueezing, Oberlin et al. 2015, 2017) corrects instantaneous frequency chirp rate, ridges follow fast changes sedimentation rate also long wavelets; type = "set" (synchroextracting transform, Yu et al. 2017); several omega_nr values give adaptive synchrosqueezing (per position wavelet lowest Renyi entropy, Sheu et al. 2017). analyse_wavelet_sst() also gained n_iter (multisynchrosqueezing, Yu et al. 2019: frequency reassignment repeated) type = "reassign" (reassigned scalogram, Auger Flandrin 1995: power moved period depth/time). New analyse_superlet_sst(): synchrosqueezed transforms wavelets increasing number cycles (default omega_0 = 8, 12, 16; second order, 4 reassignment iterations) combined geometric mean (superlet principle, Moca et al. 2021). synthetic tests (eccentricity-modulated precession obliquity, changing sedimentation rate, AR1 noise) put 75-90 % energy within 3 % true periods, 25-40 % Morlet scalogram, separated 19 23.7 kyr precession bands best. New analyse_conceft(): ConceFT multitaper synchrosqueezing orthonormal generalised Morse wavelets (Daubechies, Wang Wu 2016), method = "multitaper". New sst_significance(): significance synchrosqueezed transforms AR noise (optionally changing variance) simulation settings; non-significant coefficients removed.

Default omega_nr = 12, noise threshold "riskshrink" (universal threshold finest scales), amplitude linear colour levels plots. New fft_frequency_uncertainty() (practical 1/T Heisenberg-Gabor 1/(4 pi T) frequency uncertainty, relative uncertainty) fft_uncertainty() (uncertainty tracked cycle time model, Fourier counterpart wavelet_uncertainty()). Wavelets * analyse_wavelet() new arguments wavelet wavelet_order: besides Morlet wavelet (default, unchanged) Paul, derivative--Gaussian (DOG, e.g. Mexican hat), generalised Morse bump wavelets can used. period axis always Fourier period. reconstruction constant cone influence follow wavelet, extract_signal*(), wavelet_significance() plotting functions work new wavelets. cross-wavelet, coherence Awavelet functions still Morlet . * New analyse_wavelet_sst() (alias analyze_wavelet_sst()): wavelet synchrosqueezing transform (Daubechies et al. 2011; Thakur et al. 2013). result structure analyse_wavelet(), plot_wavelet(), tracking extraction work ; ridges cycles much thinner transform stays invertible. New functions * mesa_spectrum() plot_mesa_spectrum(): maximum entropy spectral analysis (MESA, Burg). Burg recursion base R (identical coefficients stats::ar.burg), AR order chosen FPE, AIC, MDL CAT set hand, one-sided power spectral density variance preserved, peak table prominence. * mesa_evolutive(), track_mesa(), mesa_average() plot_mesa_evolutive(): evolutive MESA one several window lengths (example 30, 40 50 m), padding window top bottom (pad) spectrum spans entire record, peak extraction every window position, dynamic-programming tracking spectral ridge, average amplitude spectrum, spectral-image plot. mesa_spectrum() also accepts single window padding. * test_tuned(), plot_test_k() test_tuned_check(): updated precession-constant test tuned records (version 3). MTM peaks (optionally several proxies pooled) assigned k+s3, k+s6, k+g5, k+g2 k+g4 wide k range (default 19.5-23.5 kyr) instead windows around AstroGeo22, pre-scan removes intervals little precession, ambiguity handling peak assignments, combined k uncertainty, Earth-Moon distance length--day conversion, two tests (spectral peaks, amplitude modulation surrogates). Works better Silurian/Devonian data. British English * WaverideR now uses British spelling primary spelling: analyse_wavelet(), analyse_superlet(), analyse_Awavelet(), analyse_Xwavelet(), analyse_Xsuperlet(), analyse_wavelet_coherence() wr_coloured_noise(). American names (analyze_*, wr_colored_noise()) remain available identical aliases share help page. Arguments American spelling also accept British synonyms (colour_brewer, colour_grid, standardise, centre_limits, normalise); original argument names keep working. Removed (overlap ‘astrochron’) * berger_periods() removed (overlaps astrochron::bergerPeriods()); compare_published() longer contains Berger et al. row data file Berger1989Periods.txt removed. * Hilbert_transform() longer exported; use astrochron::hilbert(). padded internal helper still used extract_amplitude(). Parallel computing * foreach/doSNOW replaced internal base-R parallel helper. Sequential default; run_multicore = TRUE plus new n_cores argument switch parallel . Cores capped (physical cores - 1, max 4, tasks, free RAM, CRAN limit) work done batches incremental combining memory stays bounded. Results reproducible set.seed() independent number cores. * Forked workers Linux/macOS, PSOCK workers Windows RStudio (WaverideR must installed PSOCK workers). Plot windows * New wr_open_device(): Windows-code. Interactive tracking (identify()) works Windows, macOS (XQuartz/Quartz) Linux (X11) gives clear message interactive device available. * dev_new now defaults TRUE RStudio GUI (separate window needed raster plots); override options(waverider.dev_new = ...). Integrated functions * acycle2R functions (astrochronology, Earth-Moon, COCO/eCOCO, etc.), data inst/extdata. * astroMCBchron() modBchron() print/summary/predict/plot methods memory guard. Dependencies * Removed: foreach, doSNOW, DescTools, Hmisc, Matrix, matrixStats, reshape2, truncnorm, colorednoise, trapezoid, fANCOVA, DecomposeR, rlist, RColorBrewer, colorRamps, viridis (base-R replacements). scico magick now optional (Suggests). Fixes * track_ecoco(): new interactive tracker eCOCO results, counterpart track_period(). Plot eCOCO map (pcoco, rho, …), click ridge points (click deselect) get tracked sedimentation rate depth. Points can also given table (points =) scripted, reproducible tracking, result can interpolated windows. * analyze_superlet() checked direct convolution implementation Moca et al. (2021) corrected: (1) default settings order_scaling = "none" multiplied order c1 (o = NULL used order c1 instead 1); (2) order_scaling = "power" used wrong operator precedence "quadratic" documented missing; (3) records non-zero mean trend (typical stratigraphic proxies) gave power longest periods large edge effects, linear trend (mean) now removed record standardised (detrend, standardize; use detrend = "none", standardize = FALSE old behaviour); (4) amplitudes computed sums logarithms (underflow high orders) phases circular means; (5) phase sign convention opposite analyze_wavelet(); (6) new output coi (cone influence) order, warning lowerPeriod Nyquist period. (7) additive cycle rule (mult = FALSE) now checked Moca et al. (2021): -th wavelet c1 + - 1 cycles (c1 + , order 1 differed multiplicative case); additive results change accordingly. * analyze_Xsuperlet(): order_scaling order_alpha passed analyze_superlet(); default upperPeriod/lowerPeriod values swapped; cross spectrum divided period although superlet amplitudes scale dependent; cross phase taken complex geometric mean, whose phase defined (wraps), now difference circular-mean phases. Records now trimmed common, complete part. * New wavelet_significance(): significance levels wavelet superlet scalograms. method = "analytic" instantaneous Torrence Compo (1998) red-noise test (local chi-square levels global spectrum degrees freedom; wavelets ; 4-5 percent false positives simulations Morlet omega 6, 8 10). method = "surrogate" runs noise surrogates transform (wavelets superlets) white, AR(1), signal-corrected AR(1) (candidate periods removed noise estimated) power-law backgrounds, gives scale-wise 95 percent level outside cone influence global spectrum level (Weesp analysis), optionally p-values candidate cycles. Surrogates run several cores results independent number cores. plot_wavelet() plot_superlet() new argument add_signif outline significant cells draw global level. * New wavelet_band_significance(): significance scale-averaged wavelet power (Torrence Compo 1998, section 4d) period band obliquity precession band, white AR(1) background, instantaneous points whole band lies outside cone influence. method = "exact" (default) derives null distribution eigenvalues band-averaged quadratic form, valid omega_nr, dj, band background (checked Monte Carlo 4.6-5.1 percent false positives omega 4, 6, 10 12). method = "torrence" published chi-square form; constant (decorrelation length 0.60) holds omega 6 makes test conservative larger omega (2 percent false positives omega 10), rescaled 0.6 * 6 / omega_nr default. Designed complex incomplete stratigraphic records, WaverideR enables investigation imprint astronomical forcing even suboptimal datasets.

title: Add a wavelet plot — add_wavelet
text: wavelet Wavelet object (list) created analyse_wavelet (another function returning structure, elements x, Period, Power, axis.2, coi.1 coi.2). Required (Default=NULL gives error). lowerPeriod Shortest period shown period axis, unit depth/time axis wavelet (numeric, > 0); NULL uses shortest period wavelet. Default=NULL. upperPeriod Longest period shown period axis, unit depth/time axis wavelet (numeric, > lowerPeriod); NULL uses longest period wavelet. Default=NULL. lower_depth_time Lowest depth/time value shown depth/time axis (numeric, unit record); NULL uses minimum depth/time wavelet. Default=NULL. upper_depth_time Highest depth/time value shown depth/time axis (numeric, unit record); NULL uses maximum depth/time wavelet. Default=NULL. n.levels Number colour levels power scale (integer, > 1); colour breaks quantiles wavelet power, colour covers fraction scalogram. Default=100. plot.COI Draw cone influence semi-transparent white overlay (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=TRUE. color_brewer Palette family palette_name taken, character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" "scico" (last one, except "batlowK", needs scico package). See palette_name palette names family. Default="viridis". palette_name Name colour palette power (colour) scale, character string. names valid depends color_brewer: color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", 115 hcl.colors palettes (list grDevices::hcl.pals()), example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1". color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo". color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed wr_brewer_palettes()). color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb". color_brewer = "scico" (except "batlowK" need scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO". Low power drawn first colour palette high power last. Default="viridis". plot_dir Direction depth/time axis (logical, TRUE FALSE). TRUE draws depth/time increasing away origin (e.g. borehole age increases depth); FALSE reverses depth/time axis (e.g. outcrop log 0 m base section). Default=FALSE. add_lines Curves draw top scalogram (e.g. tracked period): matrix data frame depth/time column 1 one columns period values (unit period axis) ; every period column drawn line. NULL draws none. Default=NULL. add_points input add_lines (matrix data frame, depth/time column 1, period values next columns); period columns currently also drawn lines. NULL draws none. Default=NULL. add_abline_h Positions horizontal reference lines (numeric vector, e.g. c(2, 3, 5, 6)). plot_horizontal=TRUE periods (log2-transformed internally match period axis); plot_horizontal=FALSE depth/time values. NULL draws none. Default=NULL. add_abline_v Positions vertical reference lines (numeric vector, e.g. c(2, 3, 5, 6)). plot_horizontal=TRUE depth/time values; plot_horizontal=FALSE periods (log2-transformed internally). NULL draws none. Default=NULL. plot_horizontal Orientation plot (logical, TRUE FALSE): TRUE puts depth/time x axis period y axis; FALSE puts period x axis depth/time y axis (vertical log-style composite plots). Default=TRUE. period_ticks Spacing period tick marks octaves (numeric, > 0): tick placed every period_ticks powers 2, 1 labels every power 2, 2 every second one, values 1 add intermediate ticks. Default=1. periodlab Label period axis (character string). Default="period (m)". main Main title plot (character string); NULL gives title. Default=NULL. yaxt Draw depth/time axis plot_horizontal=FALSE (character): "s" draws , "n" suppresses (see par). Ignored plot_horizontal=TRUE, period axis always drawn function . Default="s". xaxt Accepted symmetry yaxt currently used: x axis always drawn (plot_horizontal=TRUE) replaced period axis (plot_horizontal=FALSE) (character, "s" "n"). Default="s". depth_time_lab Label depth/time axis (character string). Default="depth (m)". colour_brewer British spelling color_brewer, options; given (NULL) overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

text: amtm_prewhiten function prewhitens evenly spaced series AR(p) filter whose coefficients obtained autocovariance sequence low-variance aMTM spectrum (NW = 4, K = 7, zero padding 2^(ceiling(log2(N)) + nfft_add)) Yule-Walker equations. one-step predictions minus observations form prewhitened series; first 2*order values dropped mean removed. spectrum prewhitened series can "recoloured" dividing \(|1 - \sum_j \phi_j e^{-2\pi f j \Delta t}|^2\). Translated "Python PreWhiten Filter Example" (prewhiten(), correct_spec_for_pw()) distributed amtm_signaldetect (MIT licence), based R prewhiten() routine (Wesley Burr / David Riegert).

Required (Default=NULL gives error). order Order p autoregressive (AR) prewhitening filter (integer, >= 1; series must 2*order + 2 values). Higher orders remove red-noise background also signal; first 2*order samples lost. Default=2. nw Time-bandwidth product multitaper spectrum autocovariance sequence (ACVS) computed (numeric, > 0, typically 2 4). Default=4. k Number DPSS tapers spectrum (integer, >= 1, 2*nw - 1). Default=7. nfft_add Zero-padding exponent increment (integer, >= 0): spectrum computed 2^(ceiling(log2(N)) + nfft_add) frequencies, N number samples. Larger values give finer frequency grid longer, smoother ACVS. Default=2.

what: Adaptive multitaper spectrum with background fit and periodic signal detection — amtm_spectrum
title: Adaptive multitaper spectrum with background fit and periodic signal detection — amtm_spectrum
text: amtm_spectrum function computes adaptive multitaper (aMTM) power spectral density (PSD) evenly spaced series, fits PSD background maximum likelihood several noise models, selects best model detects periodic signals dual gamma-test / harmonic F-test criterion Di Matteo et al. (2021) Salinas et al. (2025). Method: (1) Thomson's adaptively weighted multitaper PSD (Prieto's 'multitaper' implementation: unit-energy DPSS tapers, adaptive weights iterated relative change 9.5e-7, PSD rescaled integral equals variance, one-sided doubling bins except 0 Nyquist). half degrees freedom \(\alpha_k = (\sum_j w_{jk}^2)^2 / \sum_j w_{jk}^4\). (2) Background models, fitted frequency range [2NW/T, f_Nyq - 2NW/T] (user range) minimising aMTM log-likelihood \(M = 2\sum_k [\alpha_k S_k/B_k + \ln(\Gamma(\alpha_k) S_k) - \alpha_k\ln(\alpha_k S_k/B_k)]\): white noise WHT \(B = c\) (analytical), power law PL \(B = c f^{-\beta}\), bending power law BPL \(B = c f^{-\beta}/(1 + (f/f_b)^{\gamma-\beta})\), first-order autoregressive AR1 \(B = c/(1 - 2\rho\cos(\pi f/f_{Nyq}) + \rho^2)\). (3) Model selection MERIT function (default SPD_MTM) AIC (\(M + 2 n_{free}\), 0/1/1/3 free parameters besides c WHT/PL/AR1/BPL). Adjacent aMTM frequencies correlated 2W band, criteria tend favour flexible models (BPL sometimes chosen pure white noise): inspect model_stats use bkg_model force model needed. Python code minimises M scipy SLSQP (Powell) raw parameters; stats::nlminb used (log c, beta[, gamma, log fb]) bounds starting values. reach optimum PL (parameters within ~1e-5 relative); BPL R reaches lower (better) M, SLSQP can stop local minimum. (4) Gamma-test \(\gamma_k = S_k/B_k\), whose threshold taken mixture--gamma CDF built histogram (bin width 0.1) \(\alpha_k\); harmonic F-test threshold qf(conf, 2, 2K-2). frequency detected periodic signal F-test peak threshold falls inside band \(\gamma_k\) exceeds threshold band least \(NW/(2T)\) wide. Translated Python package amtm_signaldetect v1.0.6 (Hector . Salinas; functions get_amtm_specs, get_spectra_dofA, get_background_psdfit, get_gamtest_confs, get_ftest_confs, get_gftest_confpeaks) Prieto's Python 'multitaper' v1.2.0 (MTSpec, adaptspec, ftest), MIT licensed. AR1 model AIC/MERIT criteria follow IDL code SPD_MTM (Di Matteo et al., 2021). Acycle function. Cyclostratigraphic interpretation: depth series frequency axis cycles per depth unit (e.g. cycles/m depth m); period (thickness) detected cycle 1/frequency. fitted background null hypothesis "cycle": use PL/BPL/AR1 red spectra typical sedimentary proxies, treat gamma-test test excess power red background F-test test phase-coherent sinusoid. sedimentation-rate changes smear orbital lines, real Milankovitch signal depth often passes gamma-test band gives moderate F-test; inspect , use freq_range exclude trends/high frequencies, compare ratios detected periods expected orbital ratios (e.g. 405:100:~20 kyr) rather relying single detections. frequency resolution \(2NW/T\) \(T\) series length depth units.

title: Adaptive multitaper spectrum with background fit and periodic signal detection — amtm_spectrum
text: data Input record: matrix data frame depth/time column 1 (evenly spaced; rows sorted increasing depth/time) proxy value column 2 (NA/Inf values). Required (Default=NULL gives error). nw Time-bandwidth product NW multitaper spectrum (numeric, > 0, typically 2 4). Larger values give smoother spectrum lower variance coarser frequency resolution (2NW/T). Default=3. k Number DPSS tapers (integer, >= 2, 2*nw - 1); NULL uses round(2*nw - 1), Python code. Default=NULL. nfft Number FFT points, .e. zero padding (integer); NULL uses series length N (Python default); values smaller N replaced 2N+1, 'multitaper'. Default=NULL. models Background models fit (character vector, combination "WHT" (white noise), "PL" (power law), "AR1" (first-order autoregressive, red noise) "BPL" (bending power law); case-insensitive). Default=c("WHT", "PL", "AR1", "BPL"). selection Criterion used choose background model among models (character, case-insensitive): "MERIT" (MERIT goodness--fit function SPD_MTM) "AIC" (Akaike information criterion); model lowest value selected. Default="MERIT". bkg_model Background model use detection instead automatically selected one (character, one names models); NULL uses model chosen selection. Default=NULL. freq_range Frequency range used background fit detection: numeric vector c(f_low, f_high) f_low < f_high, cycles per unit column 1 data (e.g. cycles/m); NULL uses [2NW/T, f_Nyq - 2NW/T]. least 12 frequencies must fall range. Default=NULL. conf_level Confidence level gamma-test F-test thresholds used detection (numeric, strictly 0 1, e.g. 0.95 0.99). Default=0.99. prewhiten Prewhiten series AR(pw_order) filter (via amtm_prewhiten default nw=4, k=7) analysis (logical, TRUE FALSE); spectrum, fits detection made prewhitened series recoloured PSD returned prewhiten. Default=FALSE. pw_order Order AR prewhitening filter (integer, >= 1); used prewhiten=TRUE. Default=2. genplot Plot results plot_amtm_spectrum (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. verbose Print progress messages, fitted parameters model selected model (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE.

text: data Input record: matrix data frame depth/time column 1 proxy value column 2. Rows NA removed, rows sorted depth/time record linearly interpolated even spacing equal median sampling interval. Required (Default=NULL gives error). dj Spacing successive scales octaves (numeric, > 0): scales increase 2^(j * dj), 1/100 gives 100 scales per doubling period. Smaller values give finer period axis cost computation time. Default=1/100. lowerPeriod Shortest period analyse, unit depth/time column data (numeric, > 0; least twice sampling interval). Default=2. upperPeriod Longest period analyse, unit depth/time column data (numeric, > lowerPeriod; normally length record). Default=1024. verbose Print sampling interval record interpolated (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. omega_min Number oscillatory cycles Morlet wavelet (omega_0) shortest period (numeric, > 0, typically 5 6). Fewer cycles give better depth/time resolution, cycles better period resolution. Default=6. omega_max Number oscillatory cycles Morlet wavelet longest period (numeric, > 0). number cycles changes omega_min omega_max along period axis set scaling. Default=12. scaling number wavelet cycles changes omega_min (shortest period) omega_max (longest period) (character), one : "none": linear scale index, equivalent linear log2(period); "log2": linear log2(period); "linear": linear period; "sqrt": square root normalised log2(period) (fast change short periods); "quadratic": square normalised log2(period) (fast change long periods); "power": normalised log2(period) power alpha. Default="none" (first element c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power")). alpha Exponent "power" scaling (numeric, > 0); used scaling="power". text: Combines idea superlets (Moca et al. 2021) synchrosqueezing. short wavelet (cycles) follows fast changes period, instance sedimentation rate changes, smears energy broad range periods; long wavelet (many cycles) separates close periods blurs changes along record. Superlets combine set wavelets increasing number cycles geometric mean amplitudes, keeps energy agree. wavelet transforms first synchrosqueezed (first second order, see analyse_wavelet_sst), slightly smoothed along period axis, combined geometric mean. cycle present record found every order (nearly) period survives; noise squeezed different, random periods different orders strongly suppressed; ridges long wavelets lag behind change period removed short wavelets vice versa. gives sharp ridges follow changes sedimentation rate separate close cycles noisy records. defaults (orders omega_0 = 8, 12 16, second-order synchrosqueezing 4 iterations reassignment, smoothing 0.01 octave) gave concentrated best separated ridges synthetic tests eccentricity-modulated precession, obliquity, changing sedimentation rates red noise (see NEWS).

code: # \donttest{ if (interactive()) { # needs mouse input (identify()) # Use the grey_track example tracking points to anchor the grey scale data set # of Zeeden et al., (2013) to the p-0.5t la2004 solution  grey_wt <-  analyse_wavelet(    data = grey,    dj = 1/200,    lowerPeriod = 0.02,    upperPeriod = 256,    verbose = FALSE,    omega_nr = 8  ) #Use the pre-tracked grey_track curve which traced the precession cycle grey_track <- completed_series(  wavelet = grey_wt,  tracked_curve  = grey_track,  period_up  = 1.25,  period_down  = 0.75,  extrapolate = TRUE, genplot = FALSE ) # Extract precession, obliquity and eccentricity to create a synthetic insolation curve  grey_prec <- extract_signal( tracked_cycle_curve = grey_track[,c(1,2)], wavelet = grey_wt, period_up = 1.2, period_down = 0.8, add_mean = FALSE, tracked_cycle_period = 22, extract_cycle = 22, tune = FALSE, plot_residual = FALSE )  grey_obl <- extract_signal(  tracked_cycle_curve = grey_track[,c(1,2)],  wavelet = grey_wt,  period_up = 1.2,  period_down = 0.8,  add_mean = FALSE,  tracked_cycle_period = 22,  extract_cycle = 110,  tune = FALSE,  plot_residual = FALSE )  grey_ecc <- extract_signal(  tracked_cycle_curve = grey_track[,c(1,2)],  wavelet = grey_wt,  period_up = 1.25,  period_down = 0.75,  add_mean = FALSE,  tracked_cycle_period = 22,  extract_cycle = 40.8,  tune = FALSE,  plot_residual = FALSE )  insolation_extract <- cbind(grey_ecc[,1],grey_prec[,2]+grey_obl[,2]+grey_ecc[,2]+mean(grey[,2])) insolation_extract <- as.data.frame(insolation_extract) insolation_extract_mins <- min_detect(insolation_extract,pts=3)  #use the astrosignal_example to tune to which is an \cr # ETP solution (p-0.5t la2004 solution) astrosignal_example <- na.omit(astrosignal_example) astrosignal_example[,2] <- -1*astrosignal_example[,2] astrosignal <- as.data.frame(astrosignal_example)  #anchor the synthetic insolation curve extracted from the grey scale record to the insolation curve.  anchor_pts <- astro_anchor( astro_solution = astrosignal, proxy_signal = insolation_extract, proxy_min_or_max = "min", clip_astrosolution = FALSE, astrosolution_min_or_max = "min", clip_high = NULL, clip_low = NULL, extract_astrosolution  = FALSE, astro_period_up  = NULL, astro_period_down  = NULL, astro_period_cycle  = NULL, extract_proxy_signal  = FALSE, proxy_period_up  = NULL, proxy_period_down  = NULL, proxy_period_cycle  = NULL, pts=3, verbose=FALSE, #set verbose to TRUE to allow for anchoring using text feedback commands genplot=FALSE )}# }

title: Bayesian change point analysis (Ruggieri, 2013) — bayes_changepoint
text: bayes_changepoint function applies Bayesian change point algorithm Ruggieri (2013) proxy record. record modelled sequence segments, described linear regression (intercept + trend) conjugate normal / scaled-inverse-chi-square priors. algorithm calculates marginal likelihood (log form) every possible sub-interval data (Eq. 2 Ruggieri, 2013), builds partition function forward recursion (dynamic programming, Eqs. 3-4), calculates exact posterior distribution number change points (Eqs. 5-7) draws n_sim solutions (number change points, locations segment regressions) stochastic backtrace. posterior probability change point data point, posterior-mean regression model \(R^2\) returned Acycle. addition per-sample models kept, pointwise credible intervals model derived (reflect uncertainty number location change points; sampled segment uses posterior-mean regression coefficients, Acycle). Translated Acycle v3.1 bayes_cpt.m, partition_fn.m, pick_k1.m nCk.m (Mingsong Li, modified code Eric Ruggieri); default hyperparameters Acycle "Changepoint" menu (AC.m).

what: Bispectral analysis: bispectrum, biphase and squared bicoherence — bispectral_analysis
title: Bispectral analysis: bispectrum, biphase and squared bicoherence — bispectral_analysis
text: bispectral_analysis function estimates complex bispectrum \(B(f_1,f_2) = mean[X(f_1) X(f_2) conj(X(f_1+f_2))]\), biphase \(arg B\) Kim Powers (1979) magnitude-squared bicoherence (bounded [0,1]) evenly unevenly sampled series. Two estimators available: direct FFT bispectrum averaged tapered (WOSA/Welch) segments, two-dimensional hexagonal frequency-smoothed direct estimate native DFT grid. numerical domain non-redundant positive principal domain (\(k_2 \le k_1\), \(k_1+k_2\) Nyquist). estimation series cleaned (non-finite rows removed, sorted, duplicate coordinates averaged), regularised interpolation sampling irregular, detrended optionally standardised. Optional inference: analytical Beta(1,R-1) pointwise reference, pointwise Monte Carlo surrogate thresholds, global maximum-statistic surrogate test (family-wise error control full computed principal domain) using Fourier-transform (FT) phase-randomised IAAFT surrogates (Schreiber Schmitz, 1996) plus-one Monte Carlo p-values. High bicoherence indicates repeatable quadratic phase coupling \((f_1,f_2,f_1+f_2)\); evidence causality energy transfer. Translated Acycle v3.1 bispectralAnalyze.m, bispectralDefaults.m, bispectralPreprocess.m, bispectralEstimate.m bispectralSignificance.m (Mingsong Li).

code: # \donttest{ # quadratic phase coupling: f3 = f1 + f2 with phase3 = phase1 + phase2 + 0.4 set.seed(1) seg_len <- 256 n_seg <- 16 t <- 0:(seg_len * n_seg - 1) y <- numeric(length(t)) f1 <- 30 / seg_len f2 <- 17 / seg_len for (s in seq_len(n_seg)){   idx <- (s - 1) * seg_len + seq_len(seg_len)   p1 <- 2 * pi * runif(1)   p2 <- 2 * pi * runif(1)   y[idx] <- cos(2 * pi * f1 * t[idx] + p1) +     0.85 * cos(2 * pi * f2 * t[idx] + p2) +     0.65 * cos(2 * pi * (f1 + f2) * t[idx] + p1 + p2 + 0.4) +     0.18 * rnorm(seg_len) } res <- bispectral_analysis(data = cbind(t, y), n_segments = 16,   overlap = 0, detrend = "none", max_freq_bins = 256,   significance = "global", n_sim = 19, seed = 1, genplot = TRUE)  # }

title: FT and IAAFT surrogates for bispectral significance testing — bispectral_surrogate
text: bispectral_surrogate function generates null-hypothesis surrogate series. Fourier-transform (FT) phase-randomised surrogates preserve periodogram exactly (Fourier amplitudes, including DC even-length Nyquist bin) randomising phases. Iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier-transform (IAAFT) surrogates (Schreiber Schmitz, 1996) preserve observed marginal distribution exactly iteratively approach observed Fourier amplitudes; iteration stops early relative spectral error changes less 1e-10. reported relative spectral error evaluated independent positive frequencies (DC even-length Nyquist bin excluded). text: data Record analyse (matrix data frame, two columns): depth metres column 1 proxy column 2. Non-finite rows dropped, duplicated depths averaged, unevenly spaced data linearly interpolated median sample spacing (see coco_prepare_regular_data). Required, default. orbit9 nine astronomical target periods kyr (numeric vector nine distinct values: long eccentricity, four short eccentricity terms, obliquity, three precession terms), e.g. orbit9_at_age calculate_orbit9 age record. default uses present-day periods (405.7, 130.7, 123.9, 98.9, 94.9, 41.0, 23.7, 22.4 19.0 kyr). Default=orbit9_default(). sr Sedimentation rates test, cm/kyr (numeric vector, > 0); correlation computed every value. Default=seq(0.5, 20, = 0.1). pad Length (number points) every slice zero-padded periodogram (integer, least number samples longest slice); larger value gives finer frequency grid. Default=5000. red Background (red-noise) removal applied every spectrum correlation (integer): 0 removal, 1 classical AR(1) background subtracted, 2 robust AR(1) background (median-smoothed spectrum, Mann Lees 1996 style), 3 smoothed-window-average (SWA) background (needs least 33 spectral bins). Negative power subtraction set zero. Default=1. nsim Number AR(1) Monte Carlo simulations used global local p-values (integer, >= 0); 0 skips simulations, p-values pCOCO returned. Default=1000. slices Number equal-depth slices record cut; slice standardised detrended spectra averaged (integer, >= 1; every slice needs least 4 points). Default=1. method Correlation coefficient data spectrum target spectrum (character): "Pearson" "Spearman". Default=c("Pearson", "Spearman"), .e. "Pearson". max_frequency Highest frequency target spectrum enters correlation, cycles/kyr (numeric, must least highest orbital frequency max(1/orbit9)); NULL uses 1.2 * max(1/orbit9). Default=NULL. amplitude_mode amplitudes nine target sinusoids set (character): "four-group-area" fits one amplitude per group (long eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession) band areas data spectrum (Acycle default; needs target_model="coherent-nine"), "per-orbit" fits nine amplitudes spectral peak frequency, "fixed" uses fixed weights (1.0 eccentricity, 0.8 obliquity, 0.6 precession; see coco_fixed_target_weights). Default=c("four-group-area", "per-orbit", "fixed"), .e. "four-group-area". target_model target spectrum synthesised finite record (character): "coherent-nine" (spectrum sum nine sinusoids, including interference) "phase-averaged" (sum individual spectra, averaged sine cosine phase). Default=c("coherent-nine", "phase-averaged"), .e. "coherent-nine". seed Seed random number generator (integer), Monte Carlo results can reproduced; NULL leaves current random state unchanged. Default=1. batch Number Monte Carlo simulations processed together one batch (integer, >= 1); larger batches faster use memory. NULL chooses pad (4 million spectral values per batch). Default=NULL. verbose Print messages preprocessing progress Monte Carlo simulations (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=TRUE.

text: age_constraint Age constraints (anchor points, e.g. radiometric dates) modelling run: data frame 7 columns one row per constraint. Column 1: ID name (character); column 2: age (numeric, usually kyr, unit output ages); column 3: age uncertainty unit (standard deviation normal distribution, full width range uniform one); column 4: distribution age, "n" (normal) "u" (uniform); column 5: depth constraint (depth unit tracked_cycle_curve); column 6: depth uncertainty (full width range uniform distribution); column 7: distribution depth, "u" (uniform), "n" (normal) "t" (trapezoidal, column 5 holding string "min mode1 mode2 max"). Required (Default=NULL gives error). tracked_cycle_curve Re-tracked cycle uncertainty (matrix data frame, three columns): depth column 1 (metres), mean tracked frequency cycles per metre column 2 standard deviation (1 sigma) column 3, e.g. output retrack_wt_MC. Rows NA dropped curve interpolated median depth spacing. Required (Default=NULL gives error). tracked_cycle_period Duration tracked cycle kyr (single numeric value, > 0, e.g. 405 long eccentricity cycle), used turn tracked period sedimentation rate curve2time. Required (Default=NULL gives error). tracked_cycle_period_unc Uncertainty tracked_cycle_period kyr (single numeric value, >= 0): standard deviation tracked_cycle_period_unc_dist="n", half-width range "u". Required (Default=NULL gives error). tracked_cycle_period_unc_dist Distribution duration tracked cycle drawn every simulation (character): "n" normal "u" uniform. Default="n". n_simulations Number anchored age models simulate (integer, > 0). Default=20. gap_constraints Hiatuses (gaps) insert age models: data frame 4 columns one row per gap. Column 1: duration gap (kyr); column 2: uncertainty (kyr; standard deviation normal distribution, half-width range uniform one; negative draws set 0); column 3: depth gap (depth unit tracked_cycle_curve), ages shifted drawn duration; column 4: distribution, "n" (normal) "u" (uniform). NULL inserts gaps. Default=NULL. proxy_data Proxy records used check astronomical cycles preserved tuning (list matrices data frames, depth column 1, unit tracked_cycle_curve, proxy column 2); every run one record picked random, tuned simulated age model analysed analyse_wavelet. used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=NULL. cycles_check Periods kyr astronomical cycles (numeric vector) must appear peaks average wavelet spectrum tuned proxy_data simulation accepted. used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=NULL. uncer_cycles_check Tolerance period cycles_check, kyr (numeric vector length): peak counts lies within cycles_check +/- uncer_cycles_check. used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=NULL. max_runs Number rejected simulations (anchored astronomical ages match age constraints) age constraint disagrees often dropped (integer, > 0). Default=1000. run_multicore Run simulations parallel several cores (logical, TRUE FALSE). Note parallel version also checks tuned proxy data cycles cycles_check. Default=FALSE. n_cores Number cores used run_multicore=TRUE (integer); NULL uses automatic, safe number (physical cores minus one, 4, limited free memory), can changed options(waverider.n_cores = ...). Ignored run_multicore=FALSE. Results depend number cores. Default=NULL. verbose Show progress bar (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. genplot Plot age constraints (2-sigma range) mean simulated age model 2-sigma envelope depth (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. keep_nr Minimum number age constraints kept constraints dropped max_runs rejections (integer, >= 1). Default=2. keep_all_time_curves Also return generated age curves, including ones rejected modelling run, last element output list (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. dj Spacing periods wavelet transform tuned proxy data, octaves (numeric, > 0; e.g. 1/200 gives 200 periods per doubling); smaller values give finer period axis take longer. Passed analyse_wavelet; used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=1/200. lowerPeriod Shortest period wavelet transform tuned proxy data, kyr (numeric, > 0; least twice sample spacing time). Passed analyse_wavelet; used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=1. upperPeriod Longest period wavelet transform tuned proxy data, kyr (numeric, larger lowerPeriod). Passed analyse_wavelet; used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=4600. omega_nr Central angular frequency (omega_0) Morlet wavelet used tuned proxy data (numeric, > 0; larger values give better period resolution poorer depth resolution). Passed analyse_wavelet; used run_multicore=TRUE. Default=6. seed_nr Seed random number generator (integer), Monte Carlo simulations can reproduced. Default=1337. dir Direction time depth (logical): TRUE time increases depth (younger top), FALSE time decreases depth (age model reversed). Default=TRUE.

title: Cross-validated correlation coefficient (cvCOCO) analysis — cvcoco
text: cvcoco function performs bidirectional held-("cross-validated") correlation coefficient (cvCOCO) test Acycle astronomical forcing depth series. cleaned record split two folds: two contiguous halves depth midpoint (method = "blocked", Blocked cvCOCO, Acycle public default) odd even observations (method = "interleaved", Interleaved cvCOCO). fold linearly interpolated median spacing. direction one fold used training: every tested sedimentation rate energies four one-Rayleigh union bands (long eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession) leakage-corrected exact nonnegative least-squares solve finite-record 4x4 leakage matrix, rate highest spectral correlation gives four trained group amplitudes. amplitudes frozen held-fold searches sedimentation rate (validation). -rate minimum directional validation curves consensus curve. single outer stationary AR(1) Monte Carlo reproduces complete bidirectional train/validate pipeline gives global (rate-search corrected) local p-values, robust directional p-value max(pA, pB) pCOCO. Two target designs available: "four-group-coherent-nine" (four group amplitudes expanded nine zero-phase sinusoids summed coherently; Acycle cvcoco9B.m / interleavedcvcoco.m, GUI default) "four-group" (phase-averaged noncoherent four-group target; Acycle cvcoco2.m, Acycle issues confirmatory conclusion report cocoConclusionReport.m). COCO method introduced Li et al. (2018). Translated Acycle v3.1 cvcoco.m, cvcoco2.m, cvcoco9B.m, interleavedcvcoco.m, cocoConclusionReport.m helpers (Mingsong Li). function calls following helpers cocoR port (must loaded): coco_orbit_groups, detrend_linear, ml_periodogram theored_ar1_ml; , red = 3, swa_background.

title: Cross-validated correlation coefficient (cvCOCO) analysis — cvcoco
text: data Record test (matrix data frame, two columns): depth metres column 1 proxy column 2. Unsorted, duplicated irregularly spaced depths allowed (fold cleaned linearly interpolated median spacing). Required (Default=NULL gives error). orbit9 nine astronomical target periods kyr (numeric vector nine distinct, positive values): one long eccentricity, four short eccentricity, one obliquity three precession periods (groups identified descending period rank), e.g. orbit9_at_age age record. Default=c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.6820, 22.3758, 18.9519). pad Length (number points) zero-padded periodogram (non-negative integer); fold uses max(pad, n_fold), 0 means padding (Acycle GUI padding unchecked); larger value gives finer frequency grid uses memory. Default=0. sr1 Lowest sedimentation rate tested, cm/kyr (numeric, > 0). Default=1. sr2 Highest sedimentation rate tested, cm/kyr (numeric, >= sr1). Default=20. srstep Step sedimentation-rate grid, cm/kyr (numeric, > 0). Default=0.1. red Red-noise background removed every spectrum (integer): 0 none, 1 classical AR(1), 2 robust AR(1) (median-smoothed spectrum), 3 smoothed-window average (SWA). Default=0. n_sim Number AR(1) Monte Carlo simulations complete bidirectional train/validate pipeline, used p-values pCOCO (integer, 0 1e6); 0 gives deterministic curves. Default=1000. cor_method Correlation coefficient used spectral correlations (character): "Pearson" "Spearman". Default="Pearson". method record split two folds (character): "blocked" (two contiguous halves depth midpoint; Blocked cvCOCO, Acycle default) "interleaved" (odd even observations; Interleaved cvCOCO). Default="blocked". target_model Design target (character): "four-group-coherent-nine" (four group amplitudes expanded nine zero-phase sinusoids summed coherently; Acycle GUI default) "four-group" (phase-averaged, noncoherent four-group target; allowed method="blocked"). Default="four-group-coherent-nine". max_frequency Highest frequency used spectral correlations, cycles/kyr (numeric, least highest orbital frequency max(1/orbit9)); NULL uses 1.2 times highest orbital frequency. Default=NULL. batch_size Number Monte Carlo realisations processed together (positive integer; reduced automatically memory run short); larger batches faster use memory. Default=100. seed Seed random number generator (integer), Monte Carlo results can reproduced; NULL leaves current random state unchanged. Default=NULL. interleaved_phase fold first cleaned observation belongs method="interleaved" (integer): 0 odd fold, 1 even fold. Ignored method="blocked". Default=0. genplot Plot results plot_cvcoco (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. verbose Print preprocessing information show progress bar Monte Carlo simulations (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE.

title: Cross-validated correlation coefficient (cvCOCO) analysis — cvcoco
code: # \donttest{ # synthetic ETP-like series in depth (5 cm/kyr) with AR(1) noise set.seed(2) t_kyr <- seq(0, 1600, by = 2) etp <- sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 405) + 0.6 * sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 125) +   0.5 * sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 95) + 0.8 * sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 41) +   0.5 * sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 23.7) + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * t_kyr / 19) noise <- as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(length(t_kyr)), 0.5,   method = "recursive")) dat <- cbind(t_kyr * 5 / 100, etp + 0.5 * noise) res <- cvcoco(data = dat, sr1 = 2, sr2 = 10, srstep = 0.5,   n_sim = 50, seed = 1) res$consensus$best_rate #> [1] 5 res$p_robust #> [1] 0.01960784 plot_cvcoco(res)     # }

title: Dynamic (depth-varying) Gaussian band-pass filter — dynamic_filter
text: dynamic_filter function extracts cycle whose frequency changes along depth/time axis (e.g. changing sedimentation rate) using pass band follows user-defined control points. method dynamic filter Nicolas Thibault Giovanni Rizzi (2019), adapted Mingsong Li (2020) Acycle's "Frequency Stabilization" tool, deterministic form Acycle's current core: series divided sliding windows; window pass band obtained linear interpolation control points window centre (held constant beyond first/last control point), window mean-centred, tapered square root half-sample-shifted Hann window, Gaussian band-pass filtered (half-power edges lower/upper frequency, zero padded 2^nextpow2(2 * window_samples - 1)), tapered overlap-added. result divided summed Hann weights. Acycle control points clicked evolutionary spectrum; supplied arguments, e.g. built dynamic_filter_controls period curve tracked WaverideR (track_period_wavelet, completed_series). Translated Acycle v3.1 acycleDynamicFilter.m (strict core; legacy flow dynamic_filter.m / dynamic_filter_lang.m, GUI DynamicFilter.m) (Mingsong Li).

title: Dynamic (depth-varying) Gaussian band-pass filter — dynamic_filter
text: data Input series (two-column matrix data frame finite numeric values: depth/time column 1, strictly increasing regularly sampled relative spacing tolerance 1e-5, proxy value column 2; least 8 rows). Interpolate irregular data regular grid beforehand. Required (Default=NULL). controls Pass band control points, cycles per depth/time unit. Either matrix data frame columns depth, f_low, f_high optionally f_centre (unnamed columns taken order), e.g. output dynamic_filter_controls, list elements lower upper, two-column matrix [depth, frequency] (separate lower/upper boundary picks, may different depths). Depths must strictly increasing lie within data range, frequencies must > 0, f_low < f_high f_high Nyquist frequency everywhere. control points band linearly interpolated, beyond first/last point held constant; single row gives constant pass band. Gaussian response symmetric, supplied f_centre must equal (f_low + f_high) / 2 (checked). Required (Default=NULL). window_length Length sliding windows, depth/time units (numeric, > 0, record length least 8 samples). Longer windows give sharper frequency resolution follow changes pass band less closely; window two times longest period target cycle recommended. NULL uses 20% record length (Acycle GUI default). Default=NULL. step_length Step successive windows, depth/time units (numeric, > 0, half sample interval window_length). NULL uses 4 times sample interval, (record length - window_length) / 500 give 500 steps (Acycle GUI default). Default=NULL. genplot Plot data filtered signal plot_dynamic_filter (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. x_lab Label depth/time axis plot, passed plot_dynamic_filter (character). used genplot=TRUE. Default="depth". y_lab Label proxy axis plot, passed plot_dynamic_filter (character). used genplot=TRUE. Default="proxy". verbose Show progress bar windows (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE.

title: Dynamic (depth-varying) Gaussian band-pass filter — dynamic_filter
code: # \donttest{ # cycle whose period grows linearly from 5 to 15 m (changing sed. rate) depth <- seq(0, 300, by = 0.25) period <- 5 + 10 * depth / 300 phase <- 2 * pi * cumsum(1 / period) * 0.25 set.seed(1) proxy <- sin(phase) + 0.8 * sin(2 * pi * depth / 2.1) + rnorm(length(depth), sd = 0.3) ctrl <- dynamic_filter_controls(tracked = cbind(depth, period),   rel_bandwidth = 0.3, n_points = 30) res <- dynamic_filter(data = cbind(depth, proxy), controls = ctrl,   window_length = 40, step_length = 1, genplot = FALSE) plot(depth, sin(phase), type = "l") lines(res$filtered[, 1], res$filtered[, 2], col = "red")  # }

what: Dynamic noise after orbital tuning (DYNOT) — dynot
title: Dynamic noise after orbital tuning (DYNOT) — dynot
text: dynot function runs DYNOT sedimentary noise model Li et al. (2018a,b) (orbitally tuned, usually unevenly sampled) time series. Monte Carlo realisation sampling interval drawn Weibull distribution fitted (maximum likelihood) sampling intervals data (values outside [sample_min, sample_max] replaced one shared uniform draw low values one high values, Acycle), window length drawn uniformly [window_min, window_max], time-bandwidth product nw_min + k/2 , target orbital frequency f, lower upper band limits f -/+ fz * nw / window fz uniform [fz_min, fz_max]. series pchip-interpolated drawn sampling interval, linearly detrended, padded half window (pad_type) analysed legacy power decomposition (pdan.m, see pda_legacy). power-ratio curves interpolated onto regular grid, rescaled (grand mean / realisation mean) power ratio, normalised maximum 1 needed, summarized percentiles (median plus selected confidence intervals). noise 1 - power ratio. Translated Acycle v3.1 DYNOS.m (runDynot, loadDataReady, sanitizeData), dynotIterationWorker.m, dynotPercentilePlan.m, pdan.m zeropad2.m (Mingsong Li).

title: Dynamic noise after orbital tuning (DYNOT) — dynot
text: data Tuned time series (matrix data frame, numeric: time column 1, e.g. kyr, proxy value column 2; columns ignored; least 10 rows; may unevenly sampled). Rows sorted, duplicated times averaged non-finite rows removed. Required (Default=NULL). target_periods Periods target orbital cycles, time unit data (numeric vector, > 0). power within band around target frequency 1 / period summed target power. Default=c(405.6912, 130.6979, 123.8532, 98.8517, 94.8856, 40.9897, 23.6820, 22.3758, 18.9519) (nine Acycle default periods kyr). window_min, window_max Range sliding window length, time unit data (numeric, > 0, window_min <= window_max); Monte Carlo realisation draws window length uniformly range. Default=300 Default=500. nw_min Smallest time-bandwidth product multitaper spectra (numeric, >= 0.5). realisation uses nw_min + k/2, k drawn 1:(2*(nw_max-nw_min)), nw_min nw_max=nw_min. Default=2. nw_max Largest time-bandwidth product (numeric, >= nw_min); 2*(nw_max-nw_min) must integer. equal nw_min, realisations use nw_min. Default=2. pad Number points (zero-padded FFT length) multitaper spectrum (integer, > 0); larger values give finer frequency grid. Default=1000. step Step successive windows power decomposition, samples interpolated series (integer, >= 1). Default=5. n_out Number points regular output time grid onto noise curves interpolated (integer, >= 1). Default=1000. pad_type series extended half window ends analysis (numeric code): 0 padding, 1 zeros, 2 mirrored data, 3 mean end segment, 4 random normal values mean standard deviation end segment. Default=1. fz_min, fz_max Range bandwidth multiplier (numeric, > 0, fz_min <= fz_max): lower upper limits target band f -/+ fz * nw / window, fz drawn uniformly range limit realisation. Default=0.9 Default=1.2. f_min Lower frequency limit, cycles per time unit (numeric, >= 0): target band limits clipped lower edge total band used denominator power ratio. Default=0.001. f_max Upper frequency limit, cycles per time unit (numeric, > f_min): target band limits clipped upper edge total band (clipped Nyquist frequency). Default=1. sample_min Smallest simulated sampling interval, time unit (numeric, > 0, NULL). realisation interpolates series sampling interval drawn Weibull distribution fitted sampling intervals data; draws sample_min replaced one shared uniform draw [sample_min, sample_max]. NULL uses 5th percentile data sampling intervals. Default=NULL. sample_max Largest simulated sampling interval (numeric, >= sample_min, NULL); draws replaced way. NULL uses 95th percentile data sampling intervals. Default=NULL. intervals Confidence intervals noise report, percent (numeric vector, subset 50, 68, 80, 90, 95); median always reported. Default=c(50, 68, 80, 90, 95). n_sim Number Monte Carlo realisations (integer, >= 1). Default=1000. seed Seed random number generator (integer), Monte Carlo results can reproduced; NULL leaves current random state unchanged. Default=NULL. verbose Show progress bar realisations (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. genplot Plot result plot_dynot (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE.

what: Blocked eCOCO (cross-fitted evolutionary correlation coefficient) — ecoco_blocked
title: Blocked eCOCO (cross-fitted evolutionary correlation coefficient) — ecoco_blocked
text: Blocked eCOCO evaluates complete sliding validation windows astronomical targets trained strictly non-overlapping anchor windows. Four leakage-corrected orbital-group amplitudes (long eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession; groups identified descending period rank) fitted regularly spaced anchor windows (spacing anchor_fraction * window) using complete sedimentation-rate grid, expanded coherent nine-term sine target. Every validation window evaluated nearest lower-depth anchor (forward) nearest higher-depth anchor (backward) frozen weights. consensus correlation rate smaller two directional correlations; record edges available direction used (consensus_policy = "supported") window left empty ("strict"). Stationary Gaussian AR(1) Monte Carlo nulls, one per unique window interval, repeat complete anchor training frozen validation. Global p-values use null maximum complete rate grid within window, local p-values rate. pCOCO = rho * |log10(p_global)| ridge score; sedimentation-rate ridge tracked Acycle (trackEcocoRidge). Translated Acycle v3.1 ecocoCrossfitCore.m, ecoco.m (Blocked branch), ecocoWindowSpectra.m, ecocoEstimateAr1.m, ecocoPhysicalCenters.m, ecocoPhysicalWindowValues.m, cocoNonnegativeLeakageSolve.m zeropad2.m (Mingsong Li). Uses COCO helper functions package (helpers_coco.R ecoco_* functions).

text: Tracks sedimentation-rate paths per-window correlation peaks eCOCO result, following Acycle's legacy tracking routines. Peak locations (row indices n_peaks largest score values per window pass correlation, p-value orbit-count criteria) found eccpeaks.m. mode = "slices" reproduces ecocotrack.m: windows divided n_slices depth slices (sharing boundary windows); every slice path started trial rate min(sr) max(sr) steps sr_threshold, following nearest peak within sr_threshold (reference = median last five tracked rates, ecocotrackn.m method 1). Candidate paths summarised eccount.m (mean/median rate, number windows, mean rho, mean p, summed pCOCO, summed orbit count), sorted, filtered (mean rho >= rho_min, mean p <= p_track_max, summed orbit count >= norbit_min, near-duplicate solutions within sr_threshold removed) solution largest summed pCOCO kept. mode = "single" reproduces ecocotrackn.m one path started initial_sr (reference "median5" = method 1, "previous" = method 0). text: data Input series (matrix data frame two columns: depth/time column 1, proxy value column 2), preferably evenly sampled (padded series linearly interpolated astrochron::linterp). Required (Default=NULL). win Length moving EHA window, depth/time unit data (numeric, > 0, shorter record). series also padded half window ends (see padding). Required (Default=NULL). tbw Time-bandwidth product multitaper (MTM) spectra, passed eha (numeric, <= 10, e.g. 2, 3 4); larger values give smoother spectra lower frequency resolution. Required (Default=NULL). demean Remove mean window (logical). Currently used: windows always demeaned (demean=TRUE passed eha). Default=NULL. detrend Remove linear trend window (logical). Currently used: windows always detrended (detrend=TRUE passed eha). Default=NULL. upperPeriod Longest period analyse, depth/time unit data (numeric, > lowerPeriod, win); sets fmin = 1 / upperPeriod EHA top log2 period grid. Required (Default=NULL). lowerPeriod Shortest period analyse, depth/time unit data (numeric, > 0, least twice sampling interval); sets fmax = 1 / lowerPeriod bottom log2 period grid. Required (Default=NULL). pad Number points window zero-padded (integer NULL); odd values increased one, values number points per window raised , 5 * pad passed eha obtain fine low-frequency spacing. NULL uses 2 * 2^ceiling(log2(points per window)). Default=NULL. padding Values used extend series half window ends, EHA covers whole record (character): "noise" (AR(1) red noise mean, standard deviation lag-1 autocorrelation end segments; note calls set.seed()), "mean" (also "average" "avg"; mean series) "zero" (zeros). value treated "mean". title: Extract a signal using standard deviation — extract_signal_standard_deviation
code: # \donttest{ #Extract the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle from the magnetic susceptibility #record of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018) and use the Gabor # uncertainty principle to define the mathematical uncertainty of the # analysis and use a factor of that standard deviation to define # boundaries  # perform the CWT mag_wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag, dj = 1/100, lowerPeriod = 0.1, upperPeriod = 254, verbose = FALSE, omega_nr = 10)  #Track the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle in a wavelet spectra  #mag_track <- track_period_wavelet(astro_cycle = 405, #                                   wavelet=mag_wt, #                                   n.levels = 100, #                                   periodlab = "Period (metres)", #                                   x_lab = "depth (metres)", #                                   palette_name="rainbow", #                                   color_brewer="grDevices")  #Instead of tracking, the tracked solution data set mag_track_solution is used mag_track <- mag_track_solution  mag_track_complete <- completed_series(   wavelet = mag_wt,   tracked_curve = mag_track,   period_up = 1.2,   period_down = 0.8,   extrapolate = TRUE,   genplot = FALSE )  # smooth the tracking of the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle mag_track_complete <- loess_auto(time_series = mag_track_complete, genplot = FALSE, print_span = FALSE)  # extract the 405 kyr eccentricity cycle from the wavelet spectrum and use # the Gabor uncertainty principle to define the mathematical uncertainty of # the analysis and use a multiple of the derived standard deviation to define boundaries  mag_405_ecc <- extract_signal_standard_deviation( wavelet = mag_wt, tracked_cycle_curve = mag_track_complete, multi = 1, extract_cycle = 405, tracked_cycle_period = 405, add_mean = TRUE, tune = FALSE, genplot_uncertainty_wt = FALSE, genplot_extracted = FALSE, keep_editable=FALSE, palette_name="rainbow", color_brewer="grDevices" ) # }

what: Frequency uncertainty of the Fourier transform (FFT) for a record length — fft_frequency_uncertainty
title: Frequency uncertainty of the Fourier transform (FFT) for a record length — fft_frequency_uncertainty
text: Calculator frequency uncertainty Fourier based spectrum. practical resolution FFT bin spacing, inverse record length (\(\Delta f = 1/T\)). smallest frequency uncertainty possible according Heisenberg-Gabor uncertainty principle (\(\Delta t \Delta f \ge 1/(4\pi)\)) \(\Delta t = T\) \(\Delta f = 1/(4\pi T)\), factor \(4\pi\) smaller. relative uncertainty frequency f \(\Delta f / f = 1/(f T)\). record N samples sampling frequency fs, \(T = N / f_s\). Fourier counterpart wavelet_uncertainty, gives uncertainty wavelet transform. Units free: record length metres (kyr) frequencies cycles per metre (per kyr).

title: Smooth sedimentation rate curve with uncertainty from a flmw score matrix — flmw_path
text: x Output flmw (method), list elements score_mat (matrix, trial sedimentation rates rows, depths columns), depth y_axis (trial sedimentation rates). Required (default). jump_sd Smoothness curve: standard deviation relative (natural-log) change sedimentation rate 1 metre depth, scaled square root depth step (random walk) (numeric, > 0). Small values give stiff curve, large values let rate change quickly. Default=0.2. sharpness strongly score trusted (numeric, > 0): likelihood sedimentation rate exp(sharpness * score) scores 0 1. Lower values give wider credible intervals. Default=3. normalize Divide scores 99th percentile (cap 1) sharpness means every flmw method (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=TRUE. sedrate_range Prior bounds c(min, max) sedimentation rate cm/kyr (numeric vector length 2): trial rates outside range excluded. NULL uses trial rates. Default=NULL. hiatus Depths hiatuses known breaks, depth unit x (numeric vector). depths sedimentation rate may jump freely. NULL means breaks. Default=NULL. probs Cumulative probabilities credible interval limits returned every depth (numeric vector, values 0 1). Default=c(0.025, 0.16, 0.84, 0.975) (95 68 percent intervals). genplot Plot posterior probability sedimentation rate depth probable path (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. x_lab Label x-axis (depth) plot (character). Default="depth". y_lab Label y-axis (sedimentation rate) plot (character). Default="sedrate". normalise British spelling normalize (logical, TRUE FALSE); given (NULL) overrides normalize. Default=NULL.

title: Smooth sedimentation rate curve with uncertainty from a flmw score matrix — flmw_path

title: Smooth sedimentation rate curve with uncertainty from a flmw score matrix — flmw_path
code: # synthetic score matrix with a gradual change in sedimentation rate depth <- seq(0, 20, by = 0.1) rates <- seq(1, 6, by = 0.25) true_rate <- 2 + 3 * depth / 20 score <- outer(rates, true_rate, function(r, t) exp(-0.5 * ((r - t) / 0.4)^2)) set.seed(1) score <- pmin(pmax(score + matrix(rnorm(length(score), 0, 0.2), nrow(score)), 0), 1) fake <- list(score_mat = score, depth = depth, y_axis = rates) res <- flmw_path(fake) head(res$path) #> [1] 2 2 2 2 2 2

title: Gaussian band-pass filter (Acycle) — gaussian_bandpass
text: gaussian_bandpass function applies Acycle Gaussian band-pass filter regularly sampled series. value mean removed, series zero padded 10 * 2^nextpow2(n) samples multiplied Fourier domain symmetric Gaussian response centred (f_low + f_high) / 2 whose lower upper frequencies exact half-power (-3 dB, gain 1/sqrt(2)) points. amplitude envelope modulus analytic signal (MATLAB hilbert) filtered series. Gaussian parameterisation mimics Gaussian filter Analyseries 2.0 (Paillard et al., 1996), implemented K. Ramamurthy (2013) corrected L. Hinnov (2016). Translated Acycle v3.1 acycleBandpassFilter.m (method "gaussian") gaussfilter.m (Mingsong Li).

title: Gaussian band-pass filter (Acycle) — gaussian_bandpass
text: data Numeric two-column matrix data frame: depth/time column 1 (strictly increasing regularly sampled, relative spacing tolerance 1e-5; interpolate first needed) proxy value column 2; least eight rows, values finite. Required (Default=NULL). f_low Lower half-power (-3 dB) frequency pass band, cycles per unit depth/time column (numeric, > 0; e.g. 1/25 keep periods shorter 25 m). Required (Default=NULL). f_high Upper half-power (-3 dB) frequency pass band, cycles per unit depth/time column (numeric, > f_low strictly Nyquist frequency 1 / (2 * sampling interval)). Required (Default=NULL). genplot Plot demeaned data filtered signal envelope, filter response (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. x_lab Label x-axis data plot (character). Default="depth". y_lab Label y-axis data plot (character). Default="proxy".

title: Power decomposition analysis (strict evolutionary MTM band-power ratio) — pda
text: pda function calculates, moving windows, ratio multitaper (MTM) power inside set target frequency bands power inside total frequency band (power decomposition analysis, PDA; Li et al., 2016). window linearly detrended, adaptive-weighted MTM power spectral density computed explicit FFT grid, band powers obtained trapezoidal integration PSD piecewise-linear interpolation exact band limits. input divided one global scale (maximum absolute value) powers comparable windows. data must already regularly sampled (relative spacing tolerance 1e-5); sorting, interpolation padding performed. Defaults step, nfft total_band follow Acycle compatibility wrapper pda.m (one sample interval, next power two window length, DC Nyquist). Translated Acycle v3.1 acyclePowerDecomposition.m pda.m (Mingsong Li).

title: Power decomposition analysis (strict evolutionary MTM band-power ratio) — pda

title: Power decomposition analysis (strict evolutionary MTM band-power ratio) — pda
text: data Numeric two-column matrix data frame: depth/time column 1 (strictly increasing evenly spaced, relative spacing tolerance 1e-5; interpolate first needed) proxy value column 2; least eight rows, values finite. Required (Default=NULL). target_bands Target frequency bands whose summed power divided power total_band, cycles per unit depth/time column: either B x 2 matrix lower limit column 1 upper limit column 2 (rows ordered increasing lower limit, non-overlapping), numeric vector paired limits c(lower1, upper1, lower2, upper2, ...). Every band must lie inside total_band, Nyquist frequency least wide FFT resolution. Default=c(1/45, 1/25). window Length moving window (first--last coordinate span), unit depth/time column (numeric, > 0 longer record; rounded whole number sample intervals, least 8 samples). Default=500. step Distance starts successive windows, unit depth/time column (numeric, > 0; rounded whole samples). NULL uses one sample interval. Default=NULL. nw Time-bandwidth product DPSS (Slepian) tapers multitaper spectrum (numeric, >= 0.5 less half number samples per window); larger values smooth spectrum . Default=2. nfft Length FFT (even integer, least number samples per window); larger values give finer frequency grid. NULL uses next power two number samples per window. Default=NULL. total_band Total frequency band c(lower, upper) cycles per unit depth/time column (numeric vector length 2, 0 <= lower < upper <= Nyquist frequency), denominator power ratio. NULL uses c(0, Nyquist frequency). Default=NULL. genplot Plot data power ratio depth/time (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE. verbose Show progress bar windows (logical, TRUE FALSE). Default=FALSE.

title: Legacy power decomposition analysis (Acycle PDA menu / DYNOT core) — pda_legacy
text: pda_legacy function reproduces power decomposition analysis run Acycle menu "Power Decomposition Analysis" used inside DYNOT (pdan.m; Li et al., 2016). Preprocessing Acycle menu: rows NA removed, data sorted, duplicated depths replaced mean, unevenly sampled data (relative tolerance 1e-5) linearly interpolated median sampling interval, series optionally padded half window ends (zeropad2.m). window trunc(window/dt) samples data linearly detrended adaptive MTM spectrum (pmtm(x, nw, pad)) computed. Target total powers sums spectral bins selected historical proportional bin mapping (lower = ceiling(nbin*f/fNyq), upper = trunc(nbin*f/fNyq)); overlapping target bands counted . Window centers evenly spaced first coordinate + window/2 last coordinate - window/2. Translated Acycle v3.1 pdan.m, zeropad2.m, interpolate.m, findduplicate.m AC.m (menu_pda_Callback) (Mingsong Li).

(order within pair) B x 2 matrix one band per row; overlapping bands counted . Default=c(1/45, 1/25). window Length moving window unit depth/time column (numeric, > 0); window holds trunc(window / dt) samples. title: Sliding-window spectral moments (mean frequency and bandwidth) — spectral_moments
text: spectral_moments function calculates first two spectral moments, mean frequency (\(\mu_f\)) bandwidth (\(B\)), uniformly sampled series sliding window (Sinnesael et al., 2018). moments scale sedimentation rate, evolution along stratigraphic series can used detect changes sedimentation rate. Within every window (globally mean-centred) segment linearly detrended, one-sided rectangular-window periodogram computed even NFFT grid DC Nyquist frequency $$\mu_f = \sum f P(f) / \sum P(f), \quad B = \sqrt{\sum (f-\mu_f)^2 P(f) / \sum P(f)}$$ calculated. Two computational paths available, mirroring Acycle GUI (SpectralMomentsGUI.m): strict deterministic core (default; used whenever sr_mean=NULL edge_padding "none" "zero"). Translated Acycle v3.1 acycleSpectralMoments.m (Mingsong Li). window length rounded (half away zero) integer number sampling intervals, step integer number samples, NFFT = pad x window samples (+1 odd), window centres midpoints actual window coordinates. legacy path (used sr_mean given edge_padding "mirror" "mean"). Translated Acycle v3.1 spectralmoments.m zeropad2.m (Mingsong Li, based SpectralMoments_with_SR_estimation.m DetrendSignalPP.m Matthias Sinnesael). sr_mean given long-term bandwidth trend estimated overlap-add polynomial baseline model DetrendSignalPP.m (Acycle's 'poly' option) converted relative sedimentation-rate curve scaled sr_mean (\(sr = sr_{mean} B_1 / B_{trend}\), re-centred sr_mean). Acycle, trend window round(window/step_samples) bandwidth values, .e. window expressed unit depth column used number samples, smoothing depends depth unit.

code: # \donttest{ # Two cycles (40 and 10 cm period in "age" units) recorded with a # sedimentation rate that doubles halfway the record (depth in cm): the # mean frequency halves in the upper part. dt <- 0.5 depth <- seq(0, 1000, by = dt) age <- ifelse(depth <= 500, depth, 500 + (depth - 500) / 2) set.seed(1) proxy <- sin(2 * pi * age / 40) + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * age / 10) +   stats::rnorm(length(depth), sd = 0.2) sm <- spectral_moments(data = cbind(depth, proxy), window = 200,                        step = 5, pad = 5, genplot = FALSE) plot_spectral_moments(sm, x_lab = "depth (cm)")   # with a sedimentation-rate estimate (legacy path, 'poly' trend) sm_sr <- spectral_moments(data = cbind(depth, proxy), window = 200,                           step = 5, pad = 5, sr_mean = 1.5) plot_spectral_moments(sm_sr, x_lab = "depth (cm)")  # the sedimentation rate of Sinnesael et al. (2018): the obliquity line is identified at # 5 m (41 kyr at f_obl cycles/m), the bandwidth trend is anchored there; moments over a band set.seed(3) t <- seq(0, 3000, 0.5) x <- 0.8 * sin(2 * pi * t / 41) + sin(2 * pi * t / 23.7) + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * t / 405) +   0.3 * rnorm(length(t)) rate <- 0.02 + 0.01 * sin(2 * pi * t / 1500) z <- cumsum(c(0, rate[-1] * diff(t))) zg <- seq(0, max(z), 0.02) d <- data.frame(zg, approx(z, x, zg)$y) f_obl <- 1 / (41 * approx(z, rate, 5)$y)     # the obliquity line at 5 m depth sm <- spectral_moments(d, window = 5, step = 0.1, anchor = c(5, 41, f_obl),                        freq_range = c(0.1, 8), noise_floor = TRUE) plot_spectral_moments(sm, freq_max = 8)  # }

what: Smoothed Window Average (SWA) spectral background — swa_background
title: Smoothed Window Average (SWA) spectral background — swa_background
text: Estimates background power spectrum Smoothed Window Average (SWA) method Kemp (2016), refined Weedon (2020, 2022). log10 power spectrum averaged non-overlapping windows odd width (11 99 ordinates, always keeping least three complete windows). window averages linearly interpolated, two alternative extrapolations towards zero frequency. Among candidate widths/extrapolations fit fewest non-decreasing fitted steps (, case tie, smallest RMSE) selected. constant (white-noise) quadratic high-frequency tail tested, finally fit repeatedly Hanning smoothed long RMSE degrades less 1%. Translated Acycle v3.1 specswa.m (Mingsong Li, FORTRAN code Graham Weedon).

title: Power spectrum with SWA background, chi-square and FDR confidence levels — swa_spectrum
text: Calculates power spectrum, locates spectral background Smoothed Window Average (SWA) method (Kemp, 2016; Weedon, 2020, 2022) derives chi-square confidence levels False Discovery Rate (FDR) confidence levels (Benjamini Hochberg, 1995) following procedure Miller et al. (2001), correlation neighbouring spectral estimates accounted Hopkins et al. (2002). Two spectral estimators available: method = "mtm" Multi-taper spectrum (evenly spaced, zero-mean) series, SWA background swa_background. Degrees freedom = 2K (K = number tapers). SWA option Acycle spectral analysis window. Translated Acycle v3.1 spectralswafdr.m (Mingsong Li). method = "lomb" program Weedon (2020, 2022) used Acycle SWA window: lag-1 check, linear detrending, 5% cosine taper, Lomb-Scargle transform (routine PERIOD Press et al., 1992; allows unevenly spaced data data gaps), three passes Hanning spectral window (8 degrees freedom), SWA background, chi-square FDR confidence levels. Translated Acycle v3.1 specswafdr.m (Graham Weedon, Mingsong Li).

title: Track the sedimentation rate through an eCOCO map — track_ecoco
code: # synthetic eCOCO-like map: sedimentation rate increases with depth sr <- seq(1, 10, by = 0.25) depth <- seq(0, 20, by = 0.5) true_sr <- 4 + 2 * depth / 20 rho <- 0.8 * exp(-outer(sr, true_sr, "-")^2 / 0.5) ecoco <- list(sr = sr, depth = depth, rho = rho, pcoco = 2 * rho,               p_global = matrix(0.01, length(sr), length(depth)),               norbit = matrix(9, length(sr), length(depth))) # scripted tracking: points are snapped to the nearest ridge point trk <- track_ecoco(ecoco, points = data.frame(depth = c(2, 10, 18), sr = c(4.2, 5, 5.8))) trk #>   depth sedrate     rho p_global norbit   pcoco #> 1     2    4.25 0.79601     0.01      9 1.59202 #> 2    10    5.00 0.80000     0.01      9 1.60000 #> 3    18    5.75 0.79601     0.01      9 1.59202 # \donttest{ # interactive tracking (needs a graphics device with mouse input) if (interactive()) {   trk <- track_ecoco(ecoco) } # }

Required, default. window window length x track (numeric): either window length (units first column record, matched exactly) index window x$windows (integer, 1 first window length given mesa_evolutive). length matched first.
